Case1.explanation: Because self-managed Kubernetes is required, N-Cloud is excluded because it is delivered as a provider-managed cluster. Because the operator is a beginner in routing, N-Dynamic is excluded because it requires operating BGP (a routing protocol), including AS numbers, timers, and per-node peer maintenance. The recurring monthly routing cost is $0 for both feasible options, so cost does not differentiate B-VXLAN from N-Static; no strict monthly budget was stated. TCP throughput matters for handling traffic: N-Static provides 9.74 Gbps versus 8.64 Gbps for B-VXLAN, so N-Static is higher on this criterion. Provisioning time is a one-time operational cost: B-VXLAN takes 156.55 seconds versus 234.19 seconds for N-Static, making B-VXLAN faster to provision. For the stated target cluster scale of 30, routing scalability (remaining ceiling share) is also relevant: B-VXLAN retains 0.994 versus 0.85 for N-Static. The combined scores range from 0 to 1, with higher being better; B-VXLAN scores 0.869 versus 0.131 for N-Static. Therefore, choose B-VXLAN, whose main trade-off is lower TCP throughput than N-Static in exchange for faster one-time provisioning and a higher remaining scalability share.

Case5.explanation: N-Dynamic is recommended because the cluster requires automated pod-CIDR renumbering (changing the IP-address range assigned to pods without replacing routes) and transparent traffic paths. N-Cloud was eliminated because its pod range cannot be changed in place, requiring a migration, while N-Static was eliminated because automated renumbering would require manually replacing every per-node route. B-VXLAN was eliminated because VXLAN (a tunnel that encapsulates traffic) hides pod traffic inside the encapsulation, which conflicts with the transparency requirement.
